Lesson 1 of 3

Entities, value objects, and aggregates

Use identity, immutability, and transactional boundaries to decide how domain concepts should be modeled.

Start mock interview 25-35 min LLD flow Object modeling and domain relationships 4 guided stops

Why this lesson matters

Many LLD prompts become simpler when you distinguish long-lived entities from descriptive values and group consistency rules under the right aggregate root.

Find the objects with identity

Entities are the parts of the system you track over time. They deserve identifiers, lifecycle rules, and methods that enforce meaningful transitions.

Call these points out explicitly

  • Keep entity identity stable even when attributes change

    Show likely answer
    • Keep entity identity stable even when attributes change
    • Keep entity identity stable even when attributes change
    • Identify which concepts need stable identity.

  • Attach lifecycle rules to the entity that owns them

    Show likely answer

    • Attach lifecycle rules to the entity that owns them
    • Entities are the parts of the system you track over time. They deserve identifiers, lifecycle rules, and methods that enforce meaningful transitions.

  • Avoid comparing entities only by mutable fields

    Show likely answer
    • Avoid comparing entities only by mutable fields
    • Avoid comparing entities only by mutable fields
    • Entities are the parts of the system you track over time. They deserve identifiers, lifecycle rules, and methods that enforce meaningful transitions.

Choose aggregate boundaries

Place strongly consistent rules inside one aggregate and accept eventual coordination between aggregates when the workflow spans multiple owners.

Call these points out explicitly

  • Keep each aggregate small enough to update atomically

    Show likely answer
    • Keep each aggregate small enough to update atomically
    • Keep each aggregate small enough to update atomically
    • Name the aggregate root that protects each critical invariant.

  • Route mutating commands through the aggregate root

    Show likely answer
    • Route mutating commands through the aggregate root
    • Route mutating commands through the aggregate root
    • Many LLD prompts become simpler when you distinguish long-lived entities from descriptive values and group consistency rules under the right aggregate root.

  • Avoid giant roots that serialize unrelated work

    Show likely answer
    • Avoid giant roots that serialize unrelated work
    • Avoid giant roots that serialize unrelated work
    • Creating one aggregate so large that unrelated actions contend with each other.

Common pitfalls

What to avoid

  • Treating every nested type as a separate entity.
  • Allowing callers to mutate internal collections directly.
  • Creating one aggregate so large that unrelated actions contend with each other.
